## The gap

`config/validation.yaml` defines **BUD-001** (blocking): trip limit **$5,000**, category limits lodging $2,500 / meals $800. A $9,000 trip is blocked on it. But the planner-facing snapshot published **no limits at all**.

trip-planner reads `budget_rules.max_trip_total_usd` from this snapshot, got `{}`, and so showed every cap as `$0` or "cannot be checked". Its printed approval packet told an approver a **$1,238 trip was "above the budget cap"** — under the cap TPP actually enforces, it has $3,762 of headroom. Observed 2026-09-22 against a local service.

## The change

`PlannerPolicySnapshot.budget_rules`: `rule_id`, `max_trip_total_usd`, `category_limits_usd`, `blocking`. It's built by `PolicyValidator.published_budget_rules()` **from the configured `BudgetLimitRule`**, so it can't drift from what is enforced. A policy with no budget limit publishes `{}`; the planner must then say the cap can't be checked rather than assume one.

**Currency assumption, stated rather than hidden:** policy amounts carry no currency in TPP, and the planner integration submits USD, so the limits are published under the USD keys trip-planner already reads. The field description says so.

The helper lives on `PolicyValidator`, not in `policy_api.py`, which has a deliberate 1,750-line ceiling (`test_module_sizes_stay_under_threshold`). My first version put it there and crossed the limit.

## Gate

`tests/test_policy_snapshot_caps.py` (5): the trip limit and category limits match the configuration; they reach the JSON the route returns; **a changed configured limit changes the snapshot**; a policy with no budget limit publishes none.

**Deliberate breaks:** hard-coding `5000` fails 1 of 5 — the config-follow test exists precisely because the shipped config *also* says 5000, so the first draft of this gate couldn't have caught it. Publishing nothing fails 4 of 5. Revert passes.

1,270 tests pass; mypy clean (52 files); ruff clean. `test_all_dependencies_within_declared_ranges` fails identically on `main` in this environment (local venv drift); `ruff format` flags `policy_api.py` on `main` too.

## Not the whole fix

trip-planner still has to render the cap (and read `category_limits_usd`) before the packet shows the real number; its reading of `max_trip_total_usd` already exists. See trip-planner issue 1837 / PR 1849.

Refs #1588.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Policy snapshots now include configured travel budget rules.
  * Published budget information includes rule identifiers, blocking status, trip spending limits, and category limits in USD.
  * Budget details remain available after JSON serialization and reflect current configuration.
  * Empty budget information is returned when no budget policy is configured.

title: Publish the spend limits TPP enforces in the planner policy snapshot
